sections.title: Look Back (Review)
paragraphs: Pray for one another.
Read
God sent Samuel to anoint another man David as king. David was called a man after God’s own heart. David was not perfect, but he did lead God’s people along the right path.

sections.title: Look Up (New Teaching)
paragraphs: Read

After David, others became king. These kings split the nation into two parts, Israel and Judah. All the kings in Israel were bad, and they led the people away from God. Some of the kings in Judah were also bad. But some of the kings in Judah were good, and they led God’s people to a closer relationship with Him.

During these times, God sent many servants called prophets to share a message. They repeated what God said. Sometimes they spoke about future events that would happen if the people didn’t change their ways. They also warned about God’s judgment for past actions. They predicted the future virgin birth of the Messiah and that the Messiah would die on the cross to pay for the sins of all people.
Read
Let’s read some verses from the Holy Scriptures, the Bible, that relate to this story.
Isaiah 9:1–7
Isaiah 52:13 to  53:12
Read

These verses teach us that God's judgment is true — our sins have consequences, and we cannot escape them alone. But God did not leave us alone. He sent a Servant to carry the burden that we could not. Our guilt was carried by Another. Our debt was paid. That Servant is Jesus Christ, who died for our sins and rose again, so that all who trust Him should not perish, but have eternal life. This is the grace of God that saves us.
Ask
What did you learn from these Scriptures?
Think a little — how will you practice what you have learned?

sections.title: Look Forward (Obedience)
paragraphs: Do
It’s hard to accept that we can’t pay our debt of sin; that we have nothing to offer the Holy God. Let’s ask Jesus for humble hearts that rejoice in his mercy!
Ask
I hope you enjoyed this story. When can we meet again?
Do you think someone else should hear this story?
